hints: Rewrite both cotangent and tangent in terms of sine and cosine.
After combining the numerator and denominator, use $\cos^2x+\sin^2x=1$ and $\cos^2x-\sin^2x=\cos2x$.
walkthrough:
Express $\cot x$ and $\tan x$ on the left-hand side in terms of $\sin x$ and $\cos x$, using $\cot x = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x}$ and $\tan x = \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}$:
$$\text{LHS} = \dfrac{\cot x - \tan x}{\cot x + \tan x} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} - \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}}{\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} + \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}}$$

Multiply both the numerator and the denominator by the common denominator $\sin x\cos x$ to clear the compound fractions:
$$\text{LHS} = \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} - \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}\right)\sin x\cos x}{\left(\dfrac{\cos x}{\sin x} + \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos x}\right)\sin x\cos x} = \dfrac{\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x}$$

Apply the fundamental Pythagorean identity $\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x = 1$ to simplify the denominator:
$$\text{LHS} = \dfrac{\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x}{1} = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x$$

Apply the standard cosine double-angle identity $\cos 2x = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x$:
$$\text{LHS} = \cos 2x = \text{RHS}$$
(Alternatively, using $\tan x$: $\dfrac{\cot x - \tan x}{\cot x + \tan x} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{\tan x} - \tan x}{\dfrac{1}{\tan x} + \tan x} = \dfrac{1 - \tan^2 x}{1 + \tan^2 x}$. Since $1 + \tan^2 x = \sec^2 x = \dfrac{1}{\cos^2 x}$, this equals $(1 - \tan^2 x)\cos^2 x = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x = \cos 2x$).

ai_rubric.Trigonometric Identities: Expresses the LHS in terms of either $\cos x$ and $\sin x$ or in terms of $\tan x$. The final result is $\frac{\cot x-\tan x}{\cot x+\tan x}=\cos 2x$.
